questions.q: What does `strategy.matrix.node-version: [18, 20, 22]` do to a job?
options: Runs the job three times in parallel, once for each listed Node.js version
Runs the job once, installing all three Node versions simultaneously
Fails the job unless all three versions are installed on one runner
Has no effect unless combined with workflow_call
questions.explain: A matrix multiplies one job definition into a separate parallel run for every combination of listed values — here, three runs, one per Node version.

questions.q: By default, what happens if one matrix combination fails?
options: fail-fast cancels the other still-running matrix jobs
The whole workflow is deleted from the repository
The other matrix jobs are automatically retried
Nothing — fail-fast is off by default
questions.explain: fail-fast defaults to true, so GitHub cancels the remaining matrix combinations as soon as one fails, unless it's explicitly set to false.

questions.q: What trigger makes a workflow callable from another workflow?
options: workflow_call
workflow_dispatch
pull_request
repository_dispatch
questions.explain: Declaring on: workflow_call turns a workflow file into a reusable one that other workflows can invoke with uses:.

questions.q: How does a caller workflow invoke a reusable workflow?
options: With `uses:` pointing at the reusable workflow's file path, instead of a normal job body
By copying the reusable workflow's YAML directly into its own file
By triggering it manually from the Actions tab every time
Reusable workflows cannot be called from another repository
questions.explain: A job that uses: a reusable workflow's path (optionally in another repo) calls it directly, passing inputs with `with:` and secrets with `secrets:`.

questions.q: Why did Northbridge Retail turn lint-and-test.yml into a reusable workflow?
options: So storefront, its admin dashboard, and its CLI tool could all call one real definition instead of copy-pasting the same steps
Because matrix builds require reusable workflows to function at all
Because reusable workflows run faster than normal jobs
Because secrets cannot be used in a normal, non-reusable workflow
questions.explain: Reusable workflows let a team maintain shared CI logic in one place and call it from multiple repositories, instead of duplicating the same steps everywhere.
